headline: Federal law directs the Interior Department to place certain Pima County, Arizona lands into trust for the Pascua Yaqui Tribe, making them part of its reservation.
what_it_does: The law tells the Department of the Interior to take tribally owned lands in Pima County, Arizona, into trust for the Pascua Yaqui Tribe of Arizona. Once placed in trust, the land becomes part of the Pascua Yaqui Reservation. The law also allows gaming on the land taken into trust.

who_it_affects.how: The tribe's tribally owned lands in Pima County are to be held in trust by the federal government as part of its reservation.
The department is directed to carry out the transfer of the lands into trust.

who_it_affects.group: People who visit or work at any gaming operation on the new trust land
who_it_affects.how: The law permits gaming on the land, so any gaming operation there would fall under the reservation's arrangements.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on December 27, 2022. The official summary does not give a separate date for when the land transfer must be completed.
